material_findings.title: Unconditional hidden-temporary failure state is unsupported
material_findings.candidate_excerpt: On cancellation or failure the run stops, partial data stays in hidden temporary state (.~tmp~ holding directories)

independent_primary_locators.section_or_symbol: final exit RERR_PARTIAL after transfer errors

material_findings.source_evidence: For the specified 3.2.7 peers, plain --delete defaults to --delete-during, which changes destination directories before their updates. --delay-updates delays regular-file installation, not deletion or every tree change. recv_files installs the completed-file set on reaching phase 2; a file transfer error can continue, and final cleanup can still yield RERR_PARTIAL. Failure to create a holding directory explicitly discards the completed/partial file. Temporary retention is conditional, and failure is not evidence that all incomplete-run changes remain hidden.
material_findings.reason_material: The replacement gives an affirmative recovery-state guarantee in the required failure-handling paragraph. It does not limit the guarantee to retained unfinished regular-file bytes or acknowledge already applied staging changes and possible discarded temporaries. That is a consequential misdescription of what a later recovery run must reconcile. The correct no-whole-tree-transaction sentence and failed-unpublished state mitigate risk but do not make the hidden-state assertion true.
material_findings.checked_scope_correction: For this exact proposed option family, a failed or canceled stage can contain prior deletions and installed updates; some unfinished/completed temporary files may remain, conditional on option and filesystem outcomes. Keep the stage unpublished and determine its actual state before retry/reconciliation. This is an assessor claim boundary, not an edited replacement or feedback to the candidate.
material_findings.validation: Independent static reading of pinned manual and implementation executed. No rsync transfer, cancellation experiment, or fixture command executed. A prospective failure fixture should check both destination changes and retained/discarded temporary bytes under transfer and storage errors.

limitations.title: Final preview called binding without a defined drift/approval comparison
limitations.assessment: Re-running the identical preview is a recheck, and the candidate explicitly says it is not a lock. Credit critique 5 directionally; do not invent a requirement for an actual deployment or mandatory lock. Binding is ambiguous: temporal adjacency alone cannot bind mutable tree contents, and the candidate supplies no comparison/abort rule. Read it only as the latest inspectable preview for the same intended arguments, not a tree-stability guarantee. This ambiguity is recorded separately and is not a second independent material finding.

limitations.title: --max-delete trigger/exit wording is overbroad
limitations.assessment: The limit counts files or directories, and skipped deletions/error 25 occur when further removals would exceed NUM, not merely when exactly NUM removals succeed. A more important error can override 25. --max-delete=0 is correct for the specified 3.2.7 client. Its zero mode prevents deletions, not ordinary transfer writes. This small added guardrail wording issue does not independently drive FAIL.
